**Runs Kvrocks 2 · macOS and Linux** · [registry page ↗](https://doze-dev.com/registry/doze/kvrocks/)

<!-- recipe:start -->

Run a durable key-value store that any Redis client can use, with its data on
disk instead of in memory.

Apache Kvrocks speaks the Redis protocol (RESP) and stores its data in
RocksDB. It is an Apache Software Foundation project, under the Apache-2.0
licence. Pick it over [Valkey](/services/valkey/) when the data is large or
should survive a sleep and a restart: same client code, different trade-off.
Valkey is fast and in memory; Kvrocks is durable and light on RAM.

## A store

```hcl
module kvrocks "store" {
  version = 2
}
```

```sh
doze url store
# redis://store.shop.doze:6380/0
redis-cli -u "$(doze url store)" set user:42 '{"name":"Ada"}'
```

Kvrocks's own port is 6380, so it sits beside a Valkey on 6379 without a
clash. Hand it to an app by reference: `REDIS_URL = module.store.url`.

Writes are on disk: let it sleep, connect again later, and the keys are
there. `doze reset store` deletes them.

## Cache and store together

```hcl
module valkey "cache" {
  version   = 9
  maxmemory = "128mb"
}

module kvrocks "store" {
  version = 2
}
```

Each is its own server with its own address; an app reads `module.cache.url`
and `module.store.url`.

## Namespaces

A namespace is a separate keyspace with its own token. Declaring one needs a
`password`, which is the admin's:

```hcl
module kvrocks "store" {
  version  = 2
  password = "admin"

  namespace "tenant_a" { token = "tenant-a-token" }
}
```

A client that authenticates with `tenant-a-token` sees only that namespace.

<!-- recipe:end -->

## Reference

A local Apache Kvrocks server: the Redis protocol backed by RocksDB on disk. Durable and memory-frugal — a drop-in Redis API when you want persistence without holding the dataset in RAM. Supports namespaces with per-namespace tokens.

### Every field at once

<!-- ground:skip -->
```hcl
module kvrocks "store" {
  version  = 2
  port     = 6380
  workers  = 4
  password = "admin"

  settings = {
    rocksdb.block_cache_size = "256"
  }

  namespace "tenant_a" {
    token = "tenant-a-token"
  }

  namespace "tenant_b" {
    token = "tenant-b-token"
  }
}
```

### Versions you can declare

The `version =` you write is the engine's own version. Declare a series and
doze pins its newest published build, or declare an exact build. Either way it
is fetched, verified and pinned in `doze.lock`, so it never moves on its own.

| `version =` | pins (today) | exact builds |
|---|---|---|
| `2` | `2.16.0` | 20 |

### Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `version` | number | — | Engine major to run — 2. **Required.** |
| `workers` | number | — | Number of worker threads. |
| `password` | string | — | requirepass auth password (the admin namespace); required when namespaces are declared. |
| `settings` | map(string) | — | Arbitrary kvrocks.conf directives, applied verbatim. |

Every module block also takes doze's own fields: `port`, `listen`, `sleep`,
`after`, `enabled`, `routes`, `count` and `for_each`
([doze.hcl reference](/reference/doze-hcl/)).

### Nested blocks

**`namespace "<name>" { … }`** — A logical namespace with its own access token.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `token` | string | — | Auth token scoped to this namespace. **Required.** |

### Module releases

The releases of the module that provide this engine. doze picks the newest
one that fits your doze and your `version =`, and pins it in `doze.lock`;
you never write these. Older releases stay available for pinned lockfiles.

| Release | Engine versions | Platforms | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0.2.1` | 2 | 3 | **stable** |
